definition: Improving the energy efficiency of buildings, industrial processes, equipment, heating, cooling, lighting or operations.
Installing or operating solar, wind or other renewable-energy generation facilities.
Purchasing renewable electricity through supply contracts, power purchase agreements or energy attribute certificates.
Replacing fossil-fuel equipment or processes with electric technologies.
Changing fleet vehicles, transport fuels, logistics, business travel or commuting to reduce emissions.
Reducing waste, recycling, reusing resources, reducing packaging or using recycled materials.
Working with suppliers to measure or reduce their greenhouse gas emissions.
Preventing or capturing methane, refrigerant or other fugitive greenhouse gas leaks.
Measuring emissions, establishing an inventory, assessing opportunities or developing a future reduction plan.
General environmental or emissions-reduction efforts without a clearly specified action mechanism.

label: Efficient lighting and LED retrofits
definition: Replacing inefficient lighting with LEDs or improving lighting controls. Not renewable electricity generation unless a separate solar installation is explicit.

label: Heating cooling and ventilation efficiency
definition: Improving, maintaining or replacing heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, refrigeration or chiller equipment to reduce energy demand; not refrigerant leak abatement without explicit evidence.

label: Building energy controls and temperature management
definition: Building energy management systems, sensors, operating schedules, temperature setpoints and automated controls that reduce building energy consumption.

label: Building fabric and insulation
definition: Insulation, air sealing, solar shading or energy-efficient building fabric. Solar panels are generation, not solar shading.

label: IT and data centre energy efficiency
definition: Reducing electricity demand through thin clients, efficient computers, data-centre equipment replacement, server consolidation or cloud migration. Equipment replacement alone does not imply recycling.

label: Industrial process energy optimisation
definition: Reducing energy demand by optimising manufacturing processes, equipment operation, steam systems, production schedules or industrial controls. Distinct from non-energy process emissions.

label: Efficient motors pumps and drives
definition: Efficient motors, pumps, inverters and variable-speed drives or optimised pumping pressure. Not electric vehicle conversion.

label: Compressed air system efficiency
definition: Efficient air compressors, compressed-air leak repair or replacing compressed-air applications to save energy. Compressed air is not itself a fugitive greenhouse gas.

label: Waste heat and steam recovery
definition: Recovering and reusing waste heat, waste steam or thermal energy from industrial processes, cooling water or power generation.

label: Combined heat and power
definition: Combined heat and power or cogeneration that supplies useful heat and electricity together. Does not imply renewable fuel.

label: Solar electricity generation
definition: Installing or operating photovoltaic panels or solar electricity plants, including third-party-owned onsite installations. Buying renewable electricity alone is procurement.

label: Solar water heating
definition: Installing or operating solar thermal systems for water or process heating, distinct from photovoltaic electricity generation.

label: Wind electricity generation
definition: Installing, operating or expanding wind turbines or wind power plants. A wind electricity supply contract alone is procurement.

label: Renewable energy use with unspecified sourcing
definition: Explicit renewable energy use where the text does not establish whether electricity is generated onsite or purchased. Do not infer a sourcing mechanism.

label: District heating connection
definition: Replacing onsite heating fuels through a district heating supply or network connection. Do not assume the heat is renewable without explicit evidence.

label: Lower carbon fuel substitution
definition: Replacing a fuel with a lower-emission fuel such as natural gas, biogas, biomethane or biomass. Electrification is a separate mechanism; fuel substitution is not necessarily renewable.

label: Electric vehicles and mobile equipment
definition: Replacing combustion vehicles, forklifts, cranes or other mobile equipment with electric or plug-in hybrid equipment, including related charging infrastructure.

label: Vehicle and aircraft fuel efficiency
definition: Reducing vehicle or aircraft fuel use through maintenance, driving practices, idle reduction, telematics or operational performance optimisation.

label: Freight routing and modal shift
definition: Reducing freight emissions through route optimisation, shorter distances, local sourcing or shifting away from airfreight.

label: Low carbon commuting and telework
definition: Reducing employee commuting emissions through public transport, cycling, shuttle buses, remote work or hybrid work.

label: Business travel reduction and modal shift
definition: Reducing business travel emissions through videoconferencing, rail instead of air, travel restrictions or lower-emission flight classes.

label: Site closure and consolidation
definition: Closing, downsizing or consolidating offices or production sites. Boundary reductions are not necessarily technical efficiency improvements or economy-wide emissions reductions.

label: Lower carbon material substitution
definition: Substituting lower embodied-carbon materials such as low-carbon concrete, biobased plastic or lower-emission inputs. Recycled content may additionally warrant circularity.

label: Low carbon product and service design
definition: Redesigning products or services to reduce production steps, material requirements or lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions.

label: Gas flaring reduction
definition: Reducing gas flaring through reservoir management, valve repair or gas recovery. Flaring methane to avoid venting is methane abatement, not flaring reduction.

label: Lower GWP refrigerant substitution
definition: Replacing refrigerants with lower global warming potential alternatives. Distinct from improving cooling energy efficiency alone.

label: SF6 leak prevention recovery and substitution
definition: Detecting or preventing sulphur hexafluoride leaks, recovering SF6 or replacing it with lower-GWP insulating gases.

label: Battery storage replacing diesel backup
definition: Using batteries or energy storage to replace diesel generator operation. Grid-charged batteries are not necessarily renewable generation.

label: Renewable electricity retail and supply
definition: Supplying or retailing renewable electricity to customers. Not evidence of the respondent's own renewable generation or procurement for its operations.

label: Infrastructure sharing and resource avoidance
definition: Sharing telecommunications or other physical infrastructure to avoid duplicate construction and resource use.

label: Employee energy saving practices
definition: Employee awareness, training or operational behaviours that reduce energy use, distinct from financial incentives alone.
Climate-related floods, storms, wildfires, heatwaves or other extreme events threaten operations, assets or the value chain.
Long-term climate shifts such as water scarcity, changing precipitation, rising temperatures or sea-level rise threaten business.
Climate regulation, carbon pricing, reporting obligations, compliance requirements or litigation create business risks.
The low-carbon transition creates technology replacement, obsolescence or unsuccessful technology investment risks.
Climate-related shifts in demand, input prices, energy markets or customer preferences threaten business.
Climate concerns harm reputation, stakeholder trust or brand value.
More efficient use of energy, materials, water or production resources creates a business opportunity.
Renewable or low-carbon energy creates a commercial or operational opportunity.
Demand for low-carbon products, services or access to new markets creates revenue opportunities.
Climate adaptation, resilient operations or supply-chain diversification create business opportunities.
Green finance, incentives, subsidies or improved access to capital create climate-related opportunities.
Climate effects or transition measures increase operating costs, capital expenditure, compliance costs or insurance costs.
Climate effects cause lost sales, reduced demand, production disruption or lower revenue.
Climate effects damage assets, reduce asset values or cause stranded assets.
Climate opportunities increase sales, demand or revenue.
Climate actions or opportunities reduce operating costs or produce financial savings.
Insufficient money, staff, expertise or organizational capacity limits emissions-reduction initiatives.
The respondent perceives low emissions or limited remaining technical abatement potential.
Initiatives depend on a parent-company program, group decision or another organization.
Initiatives were absent in the reporting year but are planned or underway in a later period.
An explicitly dedicated budget supports emissions-reduction or energy-efficiency projects.
Projects are assessed individually using payback periods, return on investment, cost-benefit analysis or similar financial criteria.
Internal carbon prices, carbon fees or shadow prices influence investment decisions.
Employee engagement, rewards, incentives or recognition support emissions-reduction investments.
Regulatory requirements or standards drive emissions-reduction investment.
The text provides insufficient explicit information to identify the requested mechanism or explanation.
